title: The infra_failure emitter tags the agent's own text (diffs, docs, test literals, its thinking) as infrastructure
summary: The phasestream normalizer (classifyPlain and the stderr path) tags any line that matches an infra marker, tool results and diffs included. In the review replay of PR #1079, about 14 of the 19 build-pane 'infrastructure' hits were the agent's own content: diff and doc lines (`agy-model-429-...md`, `orchestrator.go:429`, a diff line number `429 +`), package notes that mention EPERM, research rows with 'rate limit', test code with "rate_limit" literals, a commit message, the agent's own 'Thought for 6.5s (... rate limit tiers ...)', `transient_regex` config text holding 'overloaded', and `panic: test timed out` (the build's own test failing). A rejected build with such a line goes uncharged for a false reason (about 8% of live rejected builds).
fix: Tag infra_failure only for lines that come from the CLI or the tool runtime, not from the agent's assistant text or from tool results that echo file content. Treat `panic: test timed out` as a code outcome, not a timeout marker. Add the `(eval):1: operation not permitted: ps` shell-startup line to the pane noise.
acceptance: A build pane whose only marker text is in a diff, a document line, a test literal or the agent's own thinking emits no infra_failure event (red today)
A real CLI or runtime error line (429, 529, a sandbox EPERM from the tool runtime) still emits one
